newsitem.title: USA: US Senate leader says 2-2.3 pct growth not enough.
newsitem.headline: US Senate leader says 2-2.3 pct growth not enough.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said Sunday U.S. growth of 2.0 to 2.3 percent was not enough and lower taxes were needed to boost the economy.

To provide greater incentive for economic growth, a capital gains tax cut would need to be broader than just for home mortgages, Lott, a Republican from Mississippi, said on CBS Television's "Face the Nation."
President Clinton "and the Fed seem to be satisfied with growth of only around two, 2.3 percent, I think that's totally inadequate," Lott said.

"We need to give some opportunity for economic growth and creation of jobs," he said. "So yes, Republicans are committed to permanent tax relief, fairness in the tax code and we're going to begin the process to get rid of the IRS (Internal Revenue Service) and have genuine tax reform for the long haul."
